image-classification.title: MNIST - Number classification
image-classification.name: MNIST - Number Classification
image-classification.summary: Handwritten digits from 0 to 9: the “hello world” of convolutional networks.

text: The MNIST database is a large database of handwritten digits. The database is widely used for training and tests in the field of machine learning.
The samples of the original NIST data sets were created "re-mixing".

The NIST training dataset was taken from the United States Census Office. In addition, NIST's black and white images were normalized to fit into a 28 x 28 pixels and softened, which introduced gray scale levels.

sections.title: Input data
items: Gray scale image and with a 28 x 28 pixels size

sections.title: Models
items: Pre-trained model: the convolutional network of the Keras example (two convolutional and two dense layers), trained with the 60,000 MNIST training images. It gets {{test_accuracy, number(style: percent; minimumFractionDigits: 1)}} of the {{test_images, number}} test images right, which it did not see during training.
Training in the browser: each training run takes 11,000 random images out of the 55,000 training images and 2,000 out of the 10,000 test images.
